docs.title: DesignBuilder Schema
docs.text: dsbxml is a Python package for reading, editing and writing DesignBuilder XML (dsbXML) files, built on Pydantic v2 and pydantic-xml. It also ships the DesignBuilder.xsd schema that defines the file format.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
pip install dsbxml

Requires Python 3.10 or later.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
from dsbxml import load_model, save_model
from dsbxml.utils import validate_against_xsd

model = load_model("path/to/model.xml")

for building in model.site.buildings.building:
    for block in building.building_blocks.building_block:
        for zone in block.zones.zone if block.zones else []:
            print(zone.body.vertices[0].coords)

model.name = "Updated model"
print(validate_against_xsd(model))  # [] if the saved file would be schema-valid
save_model(model, "output.xml")

docs.title: Zone names and floor polygons
docs.text:
from dsbxml.core import Body
from dsbxml.utils import load_model

filepath = r"samples\7.3.1.003\model from Tiago.xml"
dsb = load_model(filepath)

site = dsb.site
first_building = site.buildings.building[0]


def floor_faces(body: Body) -> list[list[list[float]]]:
    """List of floor faces, where each face is a list of x,y,z coordinates."""

    vertices = [vertex.coords for vertex in body.vertices]
    faces = []
    for surface in body.surfaces.surface:
        if surface.type == "Floor" and surface.vertex_indices:
            vertex_indices = surface.vertex_indices.rstrip(";")  # drop a trailing semicolon
            indices = [int(x) for x in vertex_indices.split(";")]
            faces.append([vertices[i] for i in indices])

    return faces


def body_title(body: Body) -> str | None:
    if body.attributes is None:
        return None
    for attribute in body.attributes.attribute:
        if attribute.key == "Title":
            return attribute.value
    return None


for block in first_building.building_blocks.building_block:
    if block.zones is None:
        continue
    for zone in block.zones.zone:
        body = zone.body
        print(body_title(body), floor_faces(body))

# if zone floor is not flat, for example has 2 surfaces or sloped

docs.title: Tables
docs.text:
Each table row is one string of #-prefixed values in field_name order. This example reads and changes a value in the Glazing table.

from dsbxml.utils import load_model

filepath = r".\samples\2026.1.0.013\Shoebox261.xml"

model = load_model(filepath)

tables = model.site.tables
glazing_table = tables.get_table_by_name("Glazing")  # KeyError if missing

# Each row is one string of "#"-prefixed values, in field_name order.
# This split assumes no value contains "#".
print(glazing_table.field_name[:5])


def read_row(row: str) -> list[str]:
    return [value.strip() for value in row.split("#")[1:]]


def write_row(values: list[str]) -> str:
    return "#" + " #".join(values)


id_column = glazing_table.field_name.index("Id")
print([read_row(row)[id_column] for row in glazing_table.row])  # every Id

values = read_row(glazing_table.row[0])
print(values[id_column])  # Id of the first row

values[id_column] = "123"  # set the Id of the first row
glazing_table.row[0] = write_row(values)
print(read_row(glazing_table.row[0])[id_column])

from dsbxml.hvac.components import HVACComponent
from dsbxml.utils import load_model


def report_set(hc: HVACComponent):
    texture = hc.image_rectangle.imageTextureIndex if hc.image_rectangle else None
    return f"{hc.__class__.__name__} | {hc.type} | {hc.componentType} | {texture}"


filepath = r".\samples\8.0.0.058\DetailedHVAC.xml"
model = load_model(filepath)

building = model.site.buildings.building[0]
hvac_network = building.hvac_network
hvac_loops = hvac_network.hvac_loops.hvac_loop

hc_set = set()
for loop in hvac_loops:
    for subloop in [loop.supply_sub_loop, loop.demand_sub_loop]:
        for hc in subloop.hvac_components.hvac_component:
            hc_set.add(report_set(hc))

for item in sorted(hc_set):
    print(item)

docs.title: Zone groups and their zones
docs.text:
from dsbxml.utils import load_model

filepath = r".\samples\2025.1.0.095\HVAC_Zones_Coloured.xml"
model = load_model(filepath)

building = model.site.buildings.building[0]


def title(attributes) -> str:
    if attributes is None:
        return "Unknown"
    return next((a.value for a in attributes.attribute if a.name == "Title"), "Unknown")


# Get all HVAC zone groups
zone_groups = building.hvac_network.hvac_zone_groups.hvac_zone_group

print(f"Found {len(zone_groups)} HVAC Zone Groups\n")
print("=" * 80)

for idx, zone_group in enumerate(zone_groups, 1):
    print(f"\n{idx}. HVAC Zone Group: {title(zone_group.zone_group_attributes)}")
    print("-" * 80)

    # Get zone components in this group
    if zone_group.zone_element_list:
        zone_components = zone_group.zone_element_list.hvac_zone_component

        if zone_components:
            print(f"   Zone Components ({len(zone_components)}):")
            for component in zone_components:
                print(f"      - {title(component.attributes)}")
                print(f"        Type: {component.type or 'Unknown type'}")
        else:
            print("   No zone components in this group")
    else:
        print("   No ZoneElementList")

    # Also show building zone handles if available
    if zone_group.building_zone_handle_list:
        zone_handles = zone_group.building_zone_handle_list.building_zone_handle
        if zone_handles:
            print(f"   Building Zone Handles: {', '.join(zone_handles)}")

print("\n" + "=" * 80)
print(f"\nTotal Zone Groups: {len(zone_groups)}")

class dsbXML(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(populate_by_name=True)

    name: str = attr()
    date: datetime.date = attr()
    version: str = attr()
    objects: str = attr()
    site: Site | None = element(tag="Site", default=None)

    @classmethod
    def from_xml(cls, source: str | bytes) -> dsbXML:  # pylint: disable=arguments-differ
        from lxml import etree

        if isinstance(source, (str, bytes)):
            # huge_tree: large models can contain a single text node over
            # libxml2's default 10 MB limit, which it otherwise refuses with
            # "xmlSAX2Characters: huge text node". DesignBuilder's own files
            # are trusted input, so lifting the limit is acceptable here.
            root = etree.fromstring(source, parser=etree.XMLParser(huge_tree=True))
        else:
            root = source

        try:
            instance = super().from_xml_tree(root)
        except ValidationError as exc:
            raise ModelValidationError(exc, root=root) from exc
        return instance

    def to_xml(self, **kwargs) -> str | bytes:
        """The model as UTF-8 XML with a declaration: bytes, or str for encoding="unicode".

        The tree is written once; it used to be written, parsed back and written again only
        to set the root's tag.
        """
        from lxml import etree

        tree_args = ("skip_empty", "exclude_none", "exclude_unset")
        tree = {k: kwargs.pop(k) for k in tree_args if k in kwargs}
        as_text = kwargs.pop("encoding", None) in ("unicode", str)
        root = self.to_xml_tree(**tree)
        root.tag = "dsbXML"
        for el in root.iter():
            if el.text == "":  # written <X/>, as a parsed tree has it
                el.text = None
        kwargs.setdefault("xml_declaration", True)
        out = etree.tostring(root, encoding="UTF-8", **kwargs)
        return out.decode("UTF-8") if as_text else bytes(out)

class AssemblyLibrary(BaseModel):
    assemblyHandle: int = attr()
    # DesignBuilder writes <AssemblyLibrary assemblyHandle="0"/> with no
    # <Assembly> children when a model has no assemblies.
    assembly: list[Assembly] = element(tag="Assembly", default_factory=list)

    @field_serializer("assemblyHandle")
    def serialize_assembly_handle(self, value: int) -> int:
        # The library's handle is the next free assembly handle, so it follows
        # the assemblies it holds. A library without assemblies keeps its own.
        if not self.assembly:
            return value
        return max(item.assemblyHandle for item in self.assembly) + 1

def validate_against_xsd(source) -> list[str]:
    """Check a model, an XML file path or XML bytes against DesignBuilder.xsd.

    Returns the schema's error messages; an empty list means the XML is valid.
    A loaded model is serialised first, so this also tells whether saving it
    would produce a file DesignBuilder's schema accepts.
    """
    from lxml import etree

    if isinstance(source, (str, Path)):
        document = etree.parse(str(source))
    else:
        xml = source if isinstance(source, bytes) else source.to_xml()
        xml = xml if isinstance(xml, bytes) else xml.encode("utf-8")
        document = etree.fromstring(xml).getroottree()
    schema = _xsd_schema()
    schema.validate(document)
    # lxml's error_log is a C extension type pylint cannot see is iterable.
    return [error.message for error in schema.error_log]  # pylint: disable=not-an-iterable

class ModelValidationError(ValueError):
    """Wraps a pydantic ValidationError, adding model context to each error.

    Falls back to pydantic's own field path when the source XML tree isn't
    available, or an error's path leaves the mapped building/zone/surface
    hierarchy (e.g. HVAC fields).
    """

    def __init__(self, original: ValidationError, root=None):
        self.original = original
        self.errors = original.errors()
        super().__init__(self._format(root))

    def _format(self, root) -> str:
        lines = [f"{len(self.errors)} validation error(s) for {self.original.title}:"]
        for error in self.errors:
            loc = error.get("loc", ())
            crumb = _breadcrumb(loc, root)
            field = loc[-1] if loc else "?"
            path = ".".join(str(part) for part in loc)
            if crumb:
                lines.append(f"  {crumb} > {field}: {error['msg']} ({path})")
            else:
                lines.append(f"  {path}: {error['msg']}")
        return "\n".join(lines)

class Point3D(BaseModel):
    value: str = "0;0;0"

    @field_validator("value", mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def _coerce_empty(cls, v):
        """Treat empty or whitespace-only text as the origin sentinel."""
        if not v or not str(v).strip():
            return "0;0;0"
        return v

    def _parse_coords(self) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
        parsed = tuple(float(c) for c in self.value.split(";"))
        if len(parsed) != 3:
            raise ValueError(f"Expected 3 coordinates, got {len(parsed)}: {self.value!r}")
        return parsed

    @property
    def x(self) -> float:
        return self._parse_coords()[0]

    @property
    def y(self) -> float:
        return self._parse_coords()[1]

    @property
    def z(self) -> float:
        return self._parse_coords()[2]

    @property
    def coords(self) -> list[float]:
        return list(self._parse_coords())

    @property
    def is_zero(self) -> bool:
        """True when all coordinates are zero — the sentinel for 'no position'."""
        return self.value == "0;0;0" or all(c == 0.0 for c in self._parse_coords())

    def __setattr__(self, name: str, value: float | list[float]) -> None:
        if name == "coords":
            if isinstance(value, list) and len(value) == 3:
                self.value = ";".join(map(str, value))
            else:
                raise ValueError("Coordinates must be a list of 3 numbers")
        elif name in ["x", "y", "z"]:
            index = {"x": 0, "y": 1, "z": 2}[name]
            coords = self.value.split(";")
            coords[index] = str(value)
            self.value = ";".join(coords)
        else:
            super().__setattr__(name, value)

    """A Point3D nested one level deeper under its own <Point3D> child tag.

class BaseModel(BaseXmlModel, search_mode=SearchMode.UNORDERED):
    """Base XML model with unordered element search.

    UNORDERED: pydantic-xml's default ORDERED mode consumes elements
    sequentially, so any field that scans past a later-appearing tag makes
    it invisible to subsequent fields. UNORDERED finds every element by tag
    name regardless of position — required because DesignBuilder XML places
    the same tags in different orders across component types.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(
        populate_by_name=True,
        validate_assignment=True,
        str_strip_whitespace=True,
        slots=True,
    )

    @classmethod
    def _built(cls) -> None:
        """Build the class's schema now if import left it for first use (see __init__.py)."""
        if cls.__xml_serializer__ is None:
            import dsbxml

            dsbxml._load_core_module()  # pylint: disable=protected-access
            cls.model_rebuild()

    @classmethod
    def from_xml_tree(cls, root, *args, **kwargs):
        cls._built()
        return super().from_xml_tree(root, *args, **kwargs)

    def to_xml_tree(self, **kwargs):
        """Serialise without unset optional values.

        pydantic-xml writes an unset optional attribute as ``name=""`` and an
        unset optional primitive element as an empty tag, both invalid
        against the schema. Empty strings and empty containers are not None
        and are still written.
        """
        kwargs.setdefault("exclude_none", True)
        type(self)._built()
        return super().to_xml_tree(**kwargs)

    def to_xml(self, **kwargs):
        """Serialise to XML text; see to_xml_tree for the unset-value handling."""
        kwargs.setdefault("exclude_none", True)
        return super().to_xml(**kwargs)

docs.text:
dsbxml loads DesignBuilder XML (dsbXML) files into typed Pydantic models, lets you read and change them in Python, and writes them back as XML.

Every Python example in this guide is run by the test suite (dsbxml/tests/test_usage_guide.py) against a real DesignBuilder model saved as building.xml, so the examples stay in step with the package. The examples build on each other: the pages run in the order listed below, and later pages use model, building and zone from earlier ones.

docs.title: Attributes
docs.text:
Most DesignBuilder settings are stored as attribute lists rather than as typed fields. The site and HVAC objects use name/value pairs (NameAttributes); buildings, blocks, bodies, surfaces and openings use key/value pairs (KeyAttributes). Values are strings, or None when the element is empty.

site_settings = {a.name: a.value for a in model.site.attributes.attribute}

building = model.site.buildings.building[0]
building_settings = {a.key: a.value for a in building.attributes.attribute}

zone = building.building_blocks.building_block[0].zones.zone[0]
zone_settings = {a.key: a.value for a in zone.body.attributes.attribute}
print(zone_settings["Title"])  # e.g. "Zone 1"

docs.title: Comparing two models
docs.text:
diff_models reports added and removed buildings, zones, surfaces and openings, changed values, and HVAC changes. Handles and indices are ignored because DesignBuilder renumbers them on every save.

from dsbxml import diff_models

before = load_model("building.xml", use_cache=False)
after = load_model("building.xml", use_cache=False)
after.name = "Renamed"

diff = diff_models(before, after)
print(diff.has_changes)  # True
print(diff.summary())    # ~ name: '...' -> 'Renamed'

  • A suffix other than .xml raises ValueError.
  • XML that does not match the models raises dsbxml.ModelValidationError (a ValueError subclass). Its message names the building, zone or surface where each problem is, and .errors holds pydantic's error list.
from dsbxml import ModelValidationError, dsbXML

try:
    dsbXML.from_xml(b'<dsbXML name="a" date="not a date" version="1" objects="all"/>')
except ModelValidationError as error:
    print(error)
    print(error.errors[0]["loc"])  # ('date',)

docs.title: Geometry
docs.text:
Coordinates are stored as "x;y;z" text in Point3D.value; the x, y, z and coords properties parse it, and assigning to them rewrites the text.

vertices = zone.body.vertices
point = vertices[0]
print(point.coords)  # [x, y, z] as floats

for point in vertices:
    print(point.x, point.y, point.z)

point.z = 3.0

docs.title: Handles
docs.text:
Objects are identified by integer handles held in their ObjectIDs. Handles read from a file are kept as they are. New ObjectIDs take the next handle from a site-wide counter, which load_model resets to the loaded site's handle; the site's handle is written back as the counter's current value.

from dsbxml.id import ObjectIDs, current_site_handle

next_handle = current_site_handle()
new_ids = ObjectIDs()
assert new_ids.handle == next_handle

The counter is a module-level global (guarded by a lock), so it is shared by every model in the process.

docs.title: HVAC
docs.text:
Detailed HVAC lives on each building's hvac_network. Buildings without detailed HVAC have an empty network, where hvac_loops is None.

for building in model.site.buildings.building:
    network = building.hvac_network
    if network is None or network.hvac_loops is None:
        continue
    for loop in network.hvac_loops.hvac_loop:
        loop_name = {a.name: a.value for a in loop.attributes.attribute}.get("Title")
        print(loop.loopType, loop_name)

docs.title: Loading and saving
docs.text:
from dsbxml import load_model, save_model

model = load_model("building.xml")

print(model.name)     # model title, e.g. "~Shoebox261"
print(model.version)  # DesignBuilder version that wrote the file
print(model.date)     # datetime.date

model.name = "Updated building"
save_model(model, "building_updated.xml")

load_model and save_model accept a str or pathlib.Path and only handle .xml files; any other suffix raises ValueError.

Loaded models are cached

load_model keeps the last 32 models in an LRU cache keyed by the file's resolved path, and returns the same object each time. A change made to one loaded model is therefore visible to every other caller that loaded the same path, and edits to the file on disk are not picked up. Pass use_cache=False to get a fresh, independent copy, or call dsbxml.utils.clear_model_cache().

from dsbxml.utils import clear_model_cache

fresh = load_model("building.xml", use_cache=False)
assert fresh is not load_model("building.xml")
clear_model_cache()

docs.title: Model structure
docs.text:
Python attribute names are snake_case versions of the XML tags; each XML container element (<Buildings>, <Zones>, ...) is a model whose list of children has the singular name:

dsbXML                      model
└── Site                    model.site
    ├── Attributes          model.site.attributes.attribute[]
    ├── Tables              model.site.tables.table[]
    ├── AssemblyLibrary     model.site.assembly_library.assembly[]
    └── Buildings           model.site.buildings.building[]
        └── Building
            ├── Attributes      building.attributes.attribute[]
            ├── BuildingBlocks  building.building_blocks.building_block[]
            │   └── BuildingBlock
            │       └── Zones   block.zones.zone[]
            │           └── Zone
            │               └── Body          zone.body
            │                   ├── Vertices  zone.body.vertices
            │                   └── Surfaces  zone.body.surfaces.surface[]
            │                       └── Surface
            │                           └── Openings  surface.openings.opening[]
            └── HVACNetwork     building.hvac_network
                ├── HVACLoops       .hvac_loops.hvac_loop[]
                └── HVACZoneGroups  .hvac_zone_groups.hvac_zone_group[]

Many elements are optional, so check for None before going deeper:

for building in model.site.buildings.building:
    for block in building.building_blocks.building_block:
        if block.zones is None:
            continue
        for zone in block.zones.zone:
            print(zone.body.volume, len(zone.body.surfaces.surface))

The schema element reference lists every element, attribute and child the file format allows; the API reference documents each Python model.

docs.title: Package imports
docs.text: dsbxml loads its model classes lazily. Every class in dsbxml.core (dsbXML, Site, Building, Zone, ...) is available from the package root, as are HVACNetwork, HVACComponents, diff_models, ModelDiff and ModelValidationError; DSB is a backwards-compatible alias for dsbXML. Classes in the other modules are imported from their module, e.g. from dsbxml.geometry import Point3D.

docs.text:
tables = model.site.tables
print([table.name for table in tables.table])

table = tables.get_table_by_name("TableOfTables")  # KeyError if missing
print(table.field_name, len(table.row))

docs.title: Validating against the schema
docs.text:
validate_against_xsd checks a loaded model, a file path or XML bytes against the DesignBuilder.xsd bundled with the package and returns the error messages; an empty list means the XML is valid. For a loaded model this tells you whether saving it would produce a file the schema accepts.

from dsbxml.utils import validate_against_xsd

errors = validate_against_xsd(model)
for message in errors:
    print(message)

Loading is more lenient than the schema: some files that do not validate still load, so validate explicitly when that matters.

Known issue: a building without detailed HVAC has an empty <HVACNetwork></HVACNetwork>, which the model writes back with an <ObjectIDs> child. The schema does not allow that, so such models report an ObjectIDs error after loading even though the source file was valid.

docs.title: Schema element reference
docs.text:
Generated from the DesignBuilder.xsd bundled with the dsbxml package (213 element names, 3316 declarations). Each section lists an element's attributes, its child elements and the elements it appears under. Where the schema declares the same element name with different content in different places, each distinct form is shown as a numbered variant.

Occurs is minOccurs..maxOccurs (* means unbounded). Group is the content model the child belongs to: sequence children must appear in the order listed, choice children are alternatives.

The schema is the contract for files DesignBuilder accepts; to check a file or a loaded model against it, use dsbxml.utils.validate_against_xsd.
